shipped_rows.title_o: Predicting defects using network analysis on dependency graphs

blind_target.evidence_quote: This paper presents a replication of one such study conducted by Zimmermann and Nagappan on Windows Server 2003 where the authors leveraged dependency relationships between software entities captured using social network metrics to predict whether they are likely to have defects.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Our results are in agreement with the original study by Zimmermann and Nagappan when using a similar experimental setup as them (random sampling). However, when we evaluated the metrics using setups more suited for industrial use -- forward-release and cross-project prediction -- we found network metrics to offer no vantage over code metrics.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The same experimental setup agrees with the original; forward-release and cross-project tests do not retain the original advantage of network metrics. Abstract lacks full target citation.

luna_triage.reason: The source explicitly calls this a replication of Zimmermann and Nagappan's Windows Server 2003 study and states its finding that network metrics outperform source-code metrics. Supplied row 222 is that same original, titled 'Predicting defects using network analysis on dependency graphs' (2008). The title/authors differ in formatting only; this is not a distinct target.
